rows.name: Constellation Software Inc.
rows.last_memo: Constellation's stock jumped about 6.5% today with no apparent reason — no earnings, no acquisition news, no management update. For a company like this, where what matters is whether management keeps buying good software businesses at attractive prices and compounding free cash f

rows.name: Deckers Outdoor Corp.
rows.last_memo: Deckers had a decent but not exceptional quarter—sales grew about 6%, the direct-to-consumer business (selling straight to shoppers, bypassing retailers) grew a healthy 13%, and international demand kept building. The downside is that spending on overhead and marketing grew much
risks: SG&A growing at 2.2x the rate of revenue in Q1 FY27; if this reflects a higher-cost operating model rather than investment spending, operating margins could structurally compress by 200-300bps versus thesis assumptions.

Inventory rose $320M in the quarter to $807.6M—a seasonal build but the absolute level warrants monitoring against sell-through data; any buildup into fiscal year-end would be a kill-criterion proximity signal.

Operating lease commitments surged ($120M of new ROU assets in one quarter vs. $45M prior year), indicating a significant retail or distribution footprint expansion; lease costs are fixed obligations that increase operating leverage in a downturn.
Tariff uncertainty explicitly mentioned in forward-looking statements; as a footwear company with overseas manufacturing, any sustained tariff escalation could structurally raise COGS.

rows.name: Microsoft Corporation
rows.last_memo: Someone uploaded 131 malicious software packages to npm, the massive public library of code that Microsoft runs through GitHub. This is a real security problem — bad actors can trick developers into downloading tainted code — but it is not unique to Microsoft; this kind of attack
risks: If AI-specific package targeting escalates, enterprise customers may impose stricter controls on open-source dependencies, marginally slowing developer adoption of Microsoft AI tooling on GitHub/Azure.

Repeated supply-chain incidents on npm could provide competitive ammunition for GitLab, JFrog Artifactory, or other alternative artifact registries seeking to displace GitHub in enterprise environments.
At $451/share, the stock now prices in ~28% long-term growth, leaving minimal margin of safety if Azure growth decelerates or AI monetization underwhelms — even modestly.

SaaS commoditization of AI features: competitive pressure (OpenAI direct, Google Gemini, Anthropic enterprise) could force Microsoft to bundle Copilot into base M365 pricing rather than sustaining $30/seat uplift, converting a margin-accretive AI monetization story into a defensive retention play.

rows.name: Alphabet Inc.
rows.last_memo: A family has filed a wrongful death lawsuit claiming YouTube's recommendation algorithm targeted their minor child with harmful content. This is serious from a human standpoint, but as an investment matter, Alphabet faces dozens of legal actions at any given time and this one doe
risks: If this lawsuit generates significant media coverage or political attention, it could accelerate existing legislative efforts (e.g., KOSA-type laws) to restrict algorithmic targeting of minors, which would constrain YouTube's ad revenue mix.
A wrongful death framing may attract plaintiff's attorneys to pursue coordinated class or mass tort litigation, increasing aggregate potential liability beyond what a single case would suggest.
Follow-on civil suits in the EU could aggregate to $10B in damages, representing a meaningful but absorbable cash outflow over multiple years.
A successful plaintiff recovery could embolden further copycat suits in other jurisdictions, increasing the total regulatory overhang.

rows.name: Amazon Com Inc.
rows.last_memo: Amazon just reported an exceptional quarter: revenue grew nearly 20% and profits grew over 40%, which means the business is becoming more efficient as it scales—exactly what the investment thesis predicted. The cloud business (AWS) is the main engine and it's accelerating, which
risks: Memory price inflation adding ~$20B to the capex program creates a near-term FCF headwind that could persist through 2026-2027 depending on DRAM/HBM market conditions.

Long-term debt doubled from $65.6B to $128.9B in six months (H1 2026 new issuance of ~$67B); while net debt/EBITDA remains well below 2.5x given earnings scale, the leverage trajectory warrants monitoring.

The $53B Q2 non-operating gain (likely Anthropic/investment mark-to-market) creates GAAP net income that dramatically overstates operating business performance; tax provision of $18B in Q2 alone suggests cash tax drag in coming periods.
Other assets surged from $122.6B to $284.1B in six months, a $161B increase likely tied to investment fair value re-measurement; if these are unrealized gains they are volatile and could reverse.

rows.name: Palantir Tech Inc.
rows.last_memo: Palantir just reported one of the most impressive quarters in its history: revenue nearly doubled year-over-year, profits tripled, and the company generated more cash in just the first half of 2026 than it did in all of the prior twelve months. The company also raised its full-ye
risks: Revenue growth comparison base becomes extremely difficult in H2 2026 and 2027, increasing risk of apparent deceleration that could compress the multiple even if absolute growth remains strong.
Customer I represents 27% of accounts receivable — concentration risk at the AR level is elevated and warrants monitoring for any single-customer slowdown.
At $125.65/share (~75x annualized FCF run-rate), the stock now prices in sustained hypergrowth; any execution stumble would be disproportionately penalized by the market.

Productizing FDE methodology risks diluting the bespoke, high-touch differentiation that drives Palantir's pricing power and customer stickiness — commoditization of the delivery model is a real second-order risk.

rows.name: Meta Platforms Inc.
rows.last_memo: Meta just told investors it plans to spend roughly $130 billion on data centers and AI hardware in 2025 — a staggering number that is about six times what the company generates in free cash flow today. To justify this, CEO Mark Zuckerberg said Meta will also sell spare computing
risks: Compute monetization strategy is unproven and puts Meta in direct competition with hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, GCP) that have significant operational and customer-relationship advantages.
If compute-sale revenue disappoints, Meta is left with $130B in annual capex commitments and no offsetting revenue stream, creating a multi-year FCF trough.
Regulatory scrutiny could intensify if Meta becomes a significant cloud/AI infrastructure provider in addition to its existing dominant social media position.
Operational complexity of running an external compute business could distract management attention from the core Family of Apps monetization.

rows.name: NVIDIA Corporation
rows.last_memo: Reports say NVIDIA may be helping to finance OpenAI's purchase of NVIDIA hardware — essentially lending money to a customer to buy your own products. On one hand, this shows just how central NVIDIA is to the AI world: the most important AI company apparently wants NVIDIA's chips
risks: Vendor financing of GPU purchases, if confirmed and material, introduces credit concentration risk to NVIDIA's balance sheet tied to OpenAI's financial health.
A pattern of vendor-financed demand would raise questions about whether AI infrastructure capex is as organically robust as current revenue growth implies.
Reputational and regulatory risk if the financing arrangement is structured in a way that regulators view as anticompetitive or as a mechanism to lock OpenAI into NVIDIA exclusively.

If Google's chip achieves commercial-scale deployment with verified 10x inference cost reduction, it could accelerate hyperscaler substitution of NVIDIA GPUs for inference workloads, compressing both volumes and ASPs in the fastest-growing AI compute segment.

rows.name: International Business Machines Corporation
rows.last_memo: IBM reported Q2 earnings and the stock went up about 1%, even though the company didn't hit its revenue target. That sounds counterintuitive, but it likely means IBM did better than expected on profits or cash flow — which are the things that actually drive IBM's long-term value.
risks: If the top-line miss reflects software or Red Hat deceleration rather than consulting/infrastructure, the primary growth engine of the thesis is impaired — this must be confirmed or ruled out via segment data.
Net debt/EBITDA at 3.47x remains above the 2.5x discipline threshold; any FCF guidance reduction would tighten this constraint materially.

Undisclosed purchase price prevents assessment of whether IBM deployed capital at a value-destructive valuation — will need disclosure to clear the kill criterion check on value-destructive acquisitions.

Quantum computing timelines are highly uncertain; if IBM escalates investment in quantum at the expense of software and hybrid cloud execution, it could distract management attention from the core thesis drivers.

rows.name: Shopify Inc.
rows.last_memo: Shopify just disclosed that orders placed by AI agents — software that can browse and buy on behalf of consumers — grew 13 times over. This is an early sign that Shopify is successfully embedding itself into the next wave of how online shopping happens, which is exactly what the
risks: Congressional probe into AI agents could result in regulatory constraints on autonomous purchasing, limiting the scale of this growth vector before it becomes financially material.
The 13x figure is a growth rate without a disclosed base — if AI orders are currently a rounding error, the signal is more marketing than substance and risks overstating the near-term opportunity.

DoorDash partnership creates a dependency on a third-party logistics network; if DoorDash changes pricing, availability, or terms, merchants enabled through this channel could face disruption with limited Shopify recourse.

Analyst downgrade, even if valuation-driven, can accelerate institutional selling and increase short-term price volatility, which matters only if Shopify needs to issue equity or if management credibility becomes tied to share price performance.

rows.name: Unitedhealth Group Inc.
rows.last_memo: The government is eliminating a subsidy that helped keep Medicare drug plan premiums low, and it takes effect in 2027. UnitedHealth runs one of the largest pharmacy benefit managers (Optum Rx), which depends heavily on Medicare drug plan economics, so this policy change hits a co
risks: Medicare Part D plan economics worsen materially in 2027 if UNH cannot reprice premiums fast enough to offset subsidy loss, pressuring both insurance and Optum pharmacy margins simultaneously.
Political framing of PBM subsidies as 'bailouts' increases the probability of further PBM-targeted legislation or CMS rulemaking adverse to Optum Rx's spread-based economics.
Senior member attrition from higher Part D premiums could reduce Optum's pharmacy dispensing volumes, adding a volume headwind on top of the margin headwind.
Federal removal of Medicare drug plan subsidy creates a structural cost shift onto Part D plan sponsors, compressing pharmacy segment margins from 2026 onward.

rows.name: Tesla Inc.
rows.last_memo: Tesla just reported earnings that disappointed investors enough to send the stock down about 15% over six days. The company's profit margins on cars have been squeezed for two years — from about 25 cents of gross profit per dollar of revenue down to about 18 cents — and this quar
risks: The magnitude of the implied value destruction ($25B) suggests guidance for 2025 or beyond may have been cut, introducing risk that consensus earnings estimates are still too high and further multiple compression is possible.
A six-day losing streak to multi-year lows increases the risk of forced selling by momentum and index-rebalancing flows, adding near-term price volatility unrelated to fundamentals.

If the earnings miss is partly attributable to Elon Musk's attention being diverted to political/governmental roles (DOGE, etc.), key-person execution risk — already a known risk — becomes more acute.

Stock-based compensation running at ~$4.6B annualized pace in 2026 represents a structural per-share dilution headwind not previously modeled at this magnitude, particularly tied to Musk's new performance grant.

rows.name: AST SpaceMobile Inc.
rows.last_memo: A Meta executive hinted that WhatsApp might work over satellite internet ahead of ASTS's next big rocket launch. The stock jumped 7.7% on the excitement. This is interesting because WhatsApp is used by billions of people in exactly the places ASTS wants to serve—emerging markets
risks: Hype-driven price appreciation disconnected from fundamentals creates downside volatility risk if BlueBird launch underperforms or the Meta tease leads to no formal agreement—sentiment unwind could be sharp.
If Meta is evaluating ASTS as a satellite partner, it is likely also evaluating Starlink Direct-to-Cell and other competitors, meaning ASTS does not have an exclusive negotiating position.
Market expectations may now be pricing in a successful Japan launch; any delay or technical underperformance in live commercial conditions could cause a sharp de-rating given the 281x P/S multiple.
A Guinness World Record is a marketing milestone, not an operational one — headline risk if the commercial launch timeline slips after this publicity push.
